summary: Web check: search hits identify ES with Erdős Problem 242 (a GitHub issue titled 'Erdős Problem 242: Erdős–Straus Proof' appears, unverified, and erdosproblems.com was not visited directly). No reusable unit-fraction Lean lemma library was identified for ES in this check.

As stated, the communication question is ill-posed: Bob's ⌊p/M⌋ plus Alice's p mod M determine p, so the content reduces to the size of a template set covering a residue class, i.e. the covering question already tracked in the dividing lane.

The query count for worst-case C is the C_min distribution: records 1,2,5,20,...,557, 23105 at p=184837; 99% quantile 9 (fingerprint #180, #183). Adaptive vs fixed order was not improved by any test here.

Character-sparse fits of f(p) are the fingerprint character-weight lane: dominant characters are the quadratic (q/p) for small q, with the q mod 3 dichotomy of the weights (fingerprint #152; H00 Z0199).

Max C_min over p is already tracked: the record sequence keeps growing (23105 at p=184837, a boundary solution; fingerprint #180). The 'unbounded C_min' question is an empirical record sequence, not a provable statement, and nothing new was computed.
Formalising 4/n certificates for n<=10^4 in Lean adds no new mathematics: finite cases are already certified by computer search. Not run.

Algebra checks out (4Ck p+1 = 1-k mod q when 4Cp ≡ -1 mod q), but the chain only gives divisibility by q, not the class condition d ≡ -1 (mod 4C'). Without a lemma closing that gap there is no test to run.
Clustering primes by bags of their certificates relabels the (C,d) data; cluster-residue alignment is the residue regression already in the fingerprint classical lane. No ES-level question is asked.

Share of solutions/primes certified by small C: 91.8% of primes ≡1(4) are certified with C<=2 and mean C_min ≈ 2 (fingerprint #183). The share of the count f(p) from small C was not separately computed.
A space-time diagram of a finite search tree has no hypothesis attached; nothing in the item is testable as an ES statement.
Grover-type speedups are a query-model statement; classical certificate search is already cheap in expectation (C_min small), so there is no ES consequence to test.
The reduction ES search ≤ factoring of the 4Cp+1 integers is standard and gives no proof content; HSP framing does not change the problem.
Complexity-class membership (PPA) of two-square finding is a relabelling; it does not give an ES lemma.
Termination of the search loop 'for c = 1,2,...' is equivalent to ES itself; the termination analyser would only restate the conjecture.

The first step is a formal observation, checked by reasoning: d | 4Cp+1 is a congruence condition on p mod d, so for any finite menu the success set is a finite union of residue classes and is b-automatic in every base. Nothing beyond the finite-menu residue structure follows.

summary: Polynomial-identity search for ES in residue classes is the Mordell/identity lane; the constraint that no polynomial identity covers square classes (Mordell–Schinzel) is in CONTEXT.md. The non-square classes are already covered by known identities.
Meet-in-the-middle over lists of size √p is not cheaper than the certificate search that is already polylog in expectation; no collision structure is stated.
A picture of the uncovered set is a visualisation without a hypothesis; the uncovered set is the residue-class complement already tracked in the dividing lane.
The finite-level projections K ∩ (Z/M) are the residue CRT-avoidance sets of the dividing lane (BRAINSTORM/z52b_dividing.md, #0310–0313): δ(X) decays like exp(-c log³X).
Same as Z1433: a Lean partnership is an engineering question; no ES mathematics is produced by it.
